text:
Sam: hey team — Sam here, started today in infra eng. Quick Q on PR etiquette: where's the canonical style guide for TS/Python? Also: preferred branch naming, commit message format, and how strict are we about squash vs multiple commits? I pushed a tiny change but my pre-commit hooks fail locally and CI blew up. who should I ping to get a reviewer?
Mira: welcome Sam :tada: — short answer: docs live at https://redwood.dev/docs/dev/PR-playbook (internal). TL;DR: branch names: feature/<ticket>-short-desc or fix/<ticket>-short. Commit messages: we use Conventional Commits (type(scope): short summary). Aim for small atomic PRs (<=200 LOC).
Mira: squash on merge is our default so don't worry about squashing locally — just make commits that make sense. We ask folks to run `pre-commit install` and `make test` before pushing. If pre-commit fails, run `pre-commit run --all-files` to see fixes.
Sam: thanks — I missed the `pre-commit install` step. Running it now. My branch is `feature/ENG-4320-logging-guardrails`. Example commit I tried: `fix(logging): prevent noisy duplicate logs when reconnecting` — is that okay?
Alex: that commit subject looks good. For scope use the package or module name (eg. `logging`). One extra note: if your change touches infra config (k8s/deploy scripts) include `infra:` scope.
Jenna: also check CODEOWNERS for files under `runtime/` — if your change modifies runtime behavior ping @Jenna and @alex for review. We try to review within 48h but smaller PRs get faster attention.
Sam: CI just posted: 
CI Bot: GitHub Actions — build #1247 failed on commit abc123. Logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/runs/1247 (fails on `pytest tests/unit/test_logging.py` with AssertionError)
Sam: ah yep, saw the failing test. Running locally to reproduce.
Mira: if it's flaky, add `@ci-fix` label and ping `#eng-oncall` or drop a short note here. For flaky tests we have a quarantine workflow: add `flaky=true` metadata and open a follow-up ticket.
Sam: re-ran tests locally, looks like my change broke an assumption. Fixing now, will push a new commit and re-run CI. Thanks for the pointers.
Alex: quick checklist I send to new hires: 
```
- run `./scripts/dev_setup.sh`
- `pre-commit install`
- `make lint` and `make test`
- branch: `feature/<JIRA>-short`
- commit: `feat(logging): add guardrail to backoff` (Conventional Commits)
- open PR with description + link to replay or eval if relevant
- add reviewers via CODEOWNERS or `@team` mention
```
Mira: tiny PR tips: include a short section "why this change" and a sentence on rollout plan. If this touches live inference paths, add an explicit rollback plan.
Jenna: one more: if you adjust API shapes, add a short compat note and update `CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased.
Sam: pushed fix, CI green now :thumbsup: — thanks everyone, will follow the playbook and ping @Mira if I hit more onboarding snags.
Mira: awesome — give the onboarding doc a quick read (setup & keys section) and drop your calendar for a 30m walkthrough if you want. Happy to pair on your first merge.
DeployBot: deploy status — no deploys triggered for branch feature/ENG-4320-logging-guardrails.
Sam: will do, appreciate the help! :heart:
